title: Sierra Healthcare — Executive Review Script (Q2 prep)
body:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working script and slide outline for the upcoming executive review with Sierra Healthcare (account tier: Strategic). Goal: align on value delivered from Redwood Inference, surface operational/technical blockers, confirm renewal posture and commercial ask, and land a path to expand Dedicated capacity for imaging/notes workloads.

Meeting audience (proposed):
- Chief Digital Officer (exec) — primary decision maker for renewal
- Head of Clinical Informatics (technical + use-case owner)
- Platform Engineering lead (infra contact)
- Product manager for AI initiatives
- Redwood: Marisol (CS lead), Elliot (solutions eng), Priya (AM)

Proposed agenda (30–40m):
1) 3m — Welcome + meeting goals (Marisol)
2) 5m — Executive summary: impact to org KPIs (Marisol)
3) 8m — Usage & performance highlights (Elliot)
4) 8m — Product roadmap + recommendations (Priya/Owen)
5) 8m — Commercial ask & renewal options (Marisol)
body_2:
Slide-by-slide script and speaker notes:
Slide 1 — Title + goals (Marisol)
- Visual: Sierra logo + Redwood logo + meeting date
- Script: "Thanks everyone for joining. Today we want to review impact from the pilot, highlight reliability and cost improvements, and propose a renewal & expansion plan that supports your Q4 deployment."
- Note: set expectations for a short technical deep-dive if infra questions come up.

Slide 2 — Executive summary (Marisol)
- Key bullets (speaker):
  - Adoption: 3 clinical teams in production; 14k monthly inference calls (avg 62k tokens/day)
  - Outcomes: 13% reduction in chart review time in pilot workflows; 8% improvement in triage accuracy (internal eval)
  - Health: Uptime 99.93% over last 90 days; mean latency 210ms for prefered model at p50, p95 580ms
- Ask: renew hosted contract with 20% reserved Dedicated capacity and a 12-month commitment to secure latency SLOs.

Slide 3 — Usage and economics (Elliot)
- Visual: small table with monthly usage, token breakdown (system/user/assistant), cost delta vs baseline (on-hosted vs dedicated)
- Speaker notes: highlight that Dedicated reduces per-inference unit cost by ~37% at current throughput and unlocks consistent 95th percentile latency target
- Talking point: "We see most volume spikes between 02:00–06:00 PT due to batch uploads from charting system; recommend scheduled burst windows + autoscaling policy to lower peak costs."

Slide 4 — Reliability & incidents (Elliot)
- List of incidents last 6 months (summary):
  - 2025-08-10: transient GPU OOM during bulk inference (mitigated by fallback to smaller quantized model) — impact < 21 minutes
  - 2025-11-22: regional throttling during peak — automated fallback to multi-region route avoided user-visible errors
- Speaker note: emphasize graceful degradation built into routing policies; show timeline and RCA ticket links.

Slide 5 — Quality/regression monitoring (Priya)
- Show alerting: regression on triage precision up 0.9% in last eval; explain snapshot evals and threshold policies.
- Action: propose a weekly guarded eval on new model variants before push to production; Redwood Optimize will run A/B checks.

Slide 6 — Technical recommendations (Owen)
- Short list:
  1) Adopt Dedicated nodes for critical triage pipeline (2x p4 equivalent)
  2) Enable KV prefix caching for repeated chart context (projected token savings: 18%)
  3) Deploy 8-bit quantized variant for batch jobs — maintain full-precision for latency-sensitive calls
- Speaker notes: include expected latency improvements and fallback plans. Mention required infra PRs: GH PR# 1832 (feature flag for prefix caching).

Slide 7 — Renewal options and commercial ask (Marisol)
- Package A (Conservative): 12 months, Hosted + burst, 20% discount, no SLA credits
- Package B (Recommended): 12 months, Dedicated base (reserved capacity) + Hosted fallback, 10% uplift vs A, includes 99.9% SLO and incident crediting
- Upsell: optional private deployment (VPC) onboarding (legal/SC review needed)
- Talking point: "We recommend Package B to lock cost and meet the latency SLOs required for clinical adoption."

Slide 8 — Risk assessment & mitigation plan (Marisol)
- Renewal risk: MEDIUM (score 6/10)
  - Drivers: budget cycles (renewal aligns with procurement in Q3), model quality sensitivity, need for formal SLOs
- Mitigations: tailored ROI deck for procurement, 30-day technical ramp for Dedicated, cross-team onboarding workshops by Redwood Solutions Eng.

Slide 9 — Implementation timeline & owners (Priya)
- 0–30 days: finalize contract (AM/Legal)
- 30–60 days: Dedicated capacity setup + private link test (Infra + RW)
- 60–120 days: Production cutover for triage pipeline + monitoring handoff
- Owners: Priya (AM) / Owen (SRE contact) / Sierra PE (TBD)

Slide 10 — Closing + asks (Marisol)
- Confirm decision maker timeline (procurement window), request a pilot 'go/no-go' checkpoint on YYYY-MM-DD (set to 2 weeks after procurement), propose a follow-up technical workshop on KV caching implementation.

Appendix — Data appendix & demo plan (Elliot)
- Demo idea: show before/after p95 latency after enabling caching using a controlled replay of 5k requests; also live compare cost-per-1k-tokens for hosted vs dedicated with current workload shape.
- Metrics to include in appendix: per-route token distribution, cost per inference, tail-latency histograms, top 10 slowest prompts and their token sizes.

Notes to self / draft fragments (informal):
- "If CDO raises procurement cost concerns, surface the 12-month TCO model comparing hosted vs dedicated. Use figure that dedicated pays back in ~7 months at current growth rate."
- Unresolved: need committed SLAs language from legal for 99.9% uptime; loop in Legal (Jira JIRA-CS-4121 assigned)
- Slack thread link for internal prep: slack: #cs-sierra-thread-2025-10 (contains notes from prior enablement)

Action items before deck freeze (owner + due date):
- Priya: Draft commercial terms for Package B and share margin sensitivity (due 2026-02-17)
- Elliot: Generate latency histograms and replay demo script (due 2026-02-20)
- Owen: Confirm GH PR#1832 deployment schedule + infra checklist (due 2026-02-18)
- Marisol: Schedule executive prep call with Sierra CDO (propose 20–30m, due 2026-02-16)

Potential pushback and rebuttals (prep bullets):
- "Why Dedicated?" -> "Dedicated gives predictable p95 latency and a lower per-inference cost at scale; we can show payback with current usage."
- "What if model accuracy drops?" -> "We keep canary rollouts and guarded evals; Redwood Optimize flags regressions and blocks rollout on threshold breaches."

Customer-specific context to weave into meeting:
- Sierra Healthcare has a compliance requirement for audit logs — emphasize Redwood Private as an option if procurement insists on VPC + KMS integration.
- They cite memory/latency concerns when processing long discharge summaries; recommend specific kernel selection and prefix caching to reduce repeated tokens.

Draft subject line for invite (email/ calendar):
- "Sierra Healthcare Executive Review — Redwood Inference (Q2 planning & renewal)"

Open questions to resolve pre-meeting:
- Legal: can we surface a conditional SLO credit for Package B? (Marisol to confirm)
- Procurement: What is Sierra's internal procurement cutoff date for Q3 budget? (Priya to ask the CDO on prep call)

References (internal):
- Confluence: sierra-healthcare-account-page (contains customer playbook + prior onboarding notes)
- GH PR#1832 (prefix caching feature flag)
- JIRA-CS-4121 (SLA/contract automation ticket)
